name: What is the difference between a low-threshold and a curbless walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a low-threshold and a curbless walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Walk-in showers can be designed with a low-profile threshold or as a completely curbless, barrier-free entry. A low-profile curb features a small lip of three to four inches that helps keep water contained while offering easier step-in access than a deep tub. A barrier-free or curbless shower eliminates the threshold entirely so the bathroom floor flows seamlessly into the shower pan. Choosing a curbless design often requires modifying or recessing the floor framing to ensure proper slope toward the drain, making it slightly more labor-intensive but ideal for aging in place or wheelchair accessibility.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low-threshold showers have a small step-over curb to catch water, while curbless showers feature a flat, barrier-free entry that requires recessed subflooring for drainage.
